conviction_note: Two of Petco's own named guidance assumptions moved in opposite directions during Q2 and management said they would roughly offset, so I net them; the residual edge is a Phase-2 IEEPA refund that guidance explicitly excludes and that a comparable pet-products importer already booked in the June quarter, plus two fresh post-June pet-category datapoints that both improved, on a 90.6M-share float with 21.5% short and no options to hedge in - modest up, well inside the 11.67% deadband because the fuel risk to the FY guide is genuine and cuts the other way.

findings.finding: Petco's Q2 and FY2026 guidance explicitly assumes NO further IEEPA tariff refunds beyond the partial one received in May 2026, yet CBP's CAPE Phase 2 opened 29 June 2026 and BARK - a pet-products importer - booked a reconciliation line item literally labelled 'IEEPA Tariffs Phase II' worth $7.363M in the quarter ended 30 June 2026, which sits entirely inside Petco's 3 May - 1 Aug fiscal Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: The sweep found a single $0.03 EPS estimate on this name - there is no sell-side machine tracking which CAPE phase disbursed when, and no WOOF note or wire item connects BARK's 6 August Phase-II disclosure to Petco's quarter. If it were priced, WOOF would not have fallen 6.9% in the week Evercore raised its target to $4 from $3.50 (31 Aug), and the June-3 sentence 'no additional refunds assumed for the balance of the year' would be quoted in previews as an explicit upside option rather than ignored. Petco's CFO quantified the direct exposure at ~7% of total merchandise COGS sourced from China/Canada/Mexico for owned brands, i.e. roughly $200M of annual import cost, so the residual refund is plausibly high-single to low-double-digit millions against a $110-112M Q2 adjusted EBITDA guide. Risk to the finding: BARK excluded its refund from adjusted EBITDA, and Petco could do the same or book it in Q3 - hence the wide band.
findings.independence: Petco's own June-3 release states the exclusion verbatim ('our outlook assumes the benefit of a partial IEEPA tariff refund received in May 2026, with no additional refunds assumed for the balance of the year') - https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/petco-reports-first-quarter-2026-results-302790636.html (2026-06-03); the CAPE Phase 2 / Phase 3 timeline and the $40bn+ disbursed by end-June is independently documented at https://www.thompsonhinesmartrade.com/2026/06/cbp-announces-phases-2-and-3-of-the-ieepa-tariff-refund-process/ and https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/06/ieepa-tariff-refund-update-government-appeals (2026-06-15); the 7% exposure figure is from CFO Sabrina Simmons via https://www.retaildive.com/news/petco-reaffirms-guidance-sales-fall-q1-tariffs/750114 (2025-06-09). NOTE: this finding and finding 2 both bear on the same June-3 Petco guidance paragraph, but the external evidence is entirely separate (CBP/BARK vs EIA/BTS diesel) - collapse the Petco release, not the two findings.
findings.why_not_priced_short: one EPS estimate on the name; nobody mapped CAPE phase timing to Petco's fiscal calendar

findings.finding: Petco's FY2026 guide is pinned to 'fuel prices remain elevated at approximately those experienced in the first quarter' - fiscal Q1 (Feb-Apr) averaged about $4.71/gal diesel on BTS monthlies ($3.72 / $4.92 / $5.50), fiscal Q2 (May-Jul) averaged about $5.20, and diesel was $5.599/gal on 31 Aug with US diesel cracks setting an all-time record above $106/bbl on 1 Sep and record-low seasonal distillate stocks going into heating season - leaving the stated H2 assumption roughly 19% below spot.
findings.why_not_priced: Petco names fuel as one of only two quantified guidance assumptions, so it is material enough to move the FY $415-430M adjusted EBITDA range, yet no WOOF-specific coverage carries a diesel number. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be trading with two Buy-side target actions in the last two weeks and no preview flagging the assumption as stale; the run-up of -10.5% over 20 days is too small and too undifferentiated to be this. Fiscal Q2 fuel was already inside the Q2 guide (management said the May refund would be 'approximately offset by incremental tariffs and higher fuel costs'), so the live risk is the H2/FY guide, not the Q2 print - which is why the band is wide and the upper bound is only mildly positive.
findings.independence: Monthly BTS diesel prints corroborate the level series independently of EIA weeklies: March $4.92 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-march-2026-0), April $5.50 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-april-2026-0), May $5.60 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-may-2026-0), July $4.96 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-july-2026-0). The record-crack / distillate-squeeze context is separately reported at https://oilprice.com/Latest-Energy-News/World-News/Diesel-Cracks-Hit-Record-Highs-as-Global-Fuel-Squeeze-Deepens.html and https://rbnenergy.com/daily-posts/blog/100bbl-diesel-crack-or-how-2026-exposed-fragility-global-refining (Sept 2026). Shares the June-3 Petco guidance paragraph with finding 1.
findings.why_not_priced_short: no WOOF coverage carries a diesel number despite fuel being a named guidance assumption

findings.finding: The two freshest independent pet-category datapoints both landed on 5 August 2026, after Petco last spoke, and both improved with raised guidance - Central Garden & Pet's Pet segment organic net sales +2% for the quarter ended 27 June 2026 with FY non-GAAP EPS raised to '$2.85 or better' from '$2.70 or better', and Freshpet net sales +15.5% to $305.6M with FY net sales growth raised to 10-12% - while Chewy, the market's default category anchor, does not report until 9 September, a week AFTER Petco.
findings.why_not_priced: The reporting order does the work: because Chewy reports 9 September, the most recent category statement any WOOF-focused reader has is Chewy's June comment that the consumer pet environment had become 'incrementally more challenged' - which is what the -10.5% 20-day drift is most plausibly discounting. Central and Freshpet contradicted that in August and neither release mentions Petco, so the read-across was never written. If it were priced, Petco's Q2 net sales guide of 'up about 0.3%, in line with consensus' would be treated as a floor rather than a ceiling, and WOOF would not have drifted lower against two upgraded pet-category guides.
findings.independence: Freshpet's raise is a separate filer and separate release: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/05/3339123/33052/en/freshpet-inc-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results.html (2026-08-05). The stale-anchor side is documented in Chewy's Q1 FY2026 call (June 2026): https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/markets-news/motley/2292259/chewy-chwy-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/ and Chewy's Q2 date confirmed for 9 Sep at https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CHWY/chewy-announces-fiscal-second-quarter-financial-results-conference-d7o4ws2alq4x.html (2026-08-19).
findings.why_not_priced_short: Chewy reports a week after Petco, so nobody has refreshed the category anchor

findings.finding: 19.51M shares are short against a float of only 90.59M - 21.5% of float and 13.46 days to cover on 1.46M average daily volume - and with the option chain unusable (ATM spread 120% of mid) shorts can only cover in the stock, into a name whose last seven prints moved +34.6%, +31.6%, +23.5%, +14.5%, +8.0%, -6.1% and -23.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced - raw short interest is on every terminal, which is why I size this small. What is not aggregated is the combination: the float is only 32% of the 285.6M shares outstanding (Scooby Aggregator holds the rest), so 21.5% of float is a far tighter constraint than the 6.8% of shares outstanding that screens report, and there is no functioning options market to absorb a hedge. If the convexity were priced there would be visible put demand or a tightening chain, and the baseline instead records a put/call OI ratio of 0.28 on 9,117 total contracts - i.e. almost nobody is expressing this in options at all.
findings.independence: A second data provider reports the same picture from a different snapshot - 19.6M shares short, 11.6% of float, 14.3 days to cover: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/796280/is-a-giant-short-squeeze-brewing-in-petco-stock . The float/ownership structure is confirmed by the controlling-stockholder language in Petco's 3 Aug 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1826470/000119312526329596/woof-20260731.htm (2026-08-03).
findings.why_not_priced_short: screens quote 6.8% of shares outstanding, not 21.5% of a 90.6M float, and there is no options market to hedge in

searched_and_found_nothing: No Petco lawsuit at the Court of International Trade found, which means CAPE Phase 3 (finally-liquidated entries, litigants only) is probably closed to them - this caps the refund upside in finding 1 to Phase 2 reconciliation entries

No 2026 WARN notice or layoff filing for Petco in California or Texas; the only hits were 2023-vintage San Diego HQ cuts (https://hoodline.com/2023/07/petco-slashes-san-diego-hq-jobs-amid-inflation-woes-increased-competition-in-a-struggling-economy/)
No 2026 Petco foot-traffic data is public - Placer.ai's free chain pages are paywalled for current periods and the newest public Petco figure is a May 2024 +3.7% YoY print

No 13D/G amendment, registration statement, secondary or take-private signal from Scooby Aggregator LP / CVC / CPPIB in the EDGAR filing list after 2026-06-01; the only ownership-adjacent event is Cameron Breitner (CVC) leaving the board 1 Aug and being replaced by Jeffrey Naylor, an independent director still deemed a Scooby designee - suggestive but I could not tie it to any transaction (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1826470/000119312526329596/woof-20260731.htm)

The refinancing/maturity-wall thesis is dead, not a finding: the 2 Feb 2026 second amendment replaced the old term loan with a $900M term loan maturing 2 Feb 2031 and $600M of 8.25% secured notes due 1 Feb 2031, the ABL had $487.6M undrawn, and the company was in covenant compliance at 2 May 2026 - so the equity is not an option on a near-term refi (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001826470/000119312526259944/woof-20260502.htm)
Q1 interest expense actually fell YoY ($32.8M vs $33.5M) despite the higher coupons, so no interest-expense surprise is building against the ~$125M FY net interest guide
No goodwill or trade-name impairment angle: Petco's annual test is in the fourth fiscal quarter and I found no evidence of an interim Q2 trigger

Holly May (CHRO) filed three Form 144s and sold 450,000 Class A shares for ~$1.15M on 7-9 July and resigned on 13 July - a real sequence, but a CHRO seat with no read-through to the quarter's numbers and already disclosed by 8-K on 17 July, so I did not file it
The 30 June annual-meeting 8-K is routine (director elections, say-on-pay, equity plan share increase, E&Y ratified) with no controlled-company vote signal available

The loyalty-programme relaunch is scheduled 'later in 2026' after a spring pilot, so it is not a Q2 comp driver (https://www.customerexperiencedive.com/news/petco-relaunch-loyalty-program-later-this-year/814601/, 2026-03-13)
Reddit r/petco and employee-forum chatter on Q2 store payroll or hours cuts returned nothing indexable
App-store review volume and rating trend for the Petco app was not retrievable

Confirmed the aggregator contamination the brief warned about: no 8-K and no IR release carries Q2 figures, Petco's own news-release index runs Halloween drop (27 Jul), board appointment (3 Aug), earnings-call notice (24 Aug) with nothing after - any '$906M net sales / $1.28 EPS' claim is an artefact
baseline_tension: It cuts against the baseline's negative fallback lean: the -10.5% 20-day drift and the run-up-derived priced_lean are most plausibly discounting Chewy's stale June category downgrade, while the two freshest category prints improved, the sell-side raised a target into the drift, the refinancing bear case is already resolved to 2031, and the only genuinely negative thing I found (diesel) is a threat to the H2 guide rather than to this quarter's number.
